newsitem.title: GREECE: Canada gold firm may suspend Greek project.
newsitem.headline: Canada gold firm may suspend Greek project.

text.p: Canada's TVX Gold Inc will suspend its multi-million-dollar project in northern Greece this month if local residents continue to disrupt work, a company official was quoted as saying on Tuesday.

"The company is scheduled to suspend the operation of the mines if the road (to the mines) does not open before the end of October," TVX executive vice-president in Greece, Costas Sinis, was quoted as saying in the Greek media.
He made the comments at a regional council meeting on the matter near Chalkidiki, where a gold processing plant has been prevented from starting work for the past 10 months by residents.
The residents have blocked the road leading to the mines, saying the processing plant would threaten the area's tourism business and the environment.
TVX has repeatedly asked the government to remove road blocks.
Sinis said the company had lost about $28 million from the delay and that it had so far paid its 600 workers without making any profits.
Company officials in Greece confirmed to Reuters that Sinis gave the warning, but he was unavailable for comment. TVX was likely to issue a statement in Canada during the day, the officials said.
TVX bought the two mines in December 1995 and agreed to build a gold processing plant in a $270 million investment, the biggest in Greece for the past three decades.
TVX president John Hick issued similar warnings at an Athens news conference earlier this year. The government said at the time it would act to ensure TVX operations proceeded normally.
The mines have proven reserves of 10.8 million tonnes of mixed sulphur minerals, of which 9.8 million contain gold.
Greek government officials told Reuters TVX could extract as much as five tonnes of gold and a half a tonne of silver annually.
